title: Documentation and Change Records
summary: Create accurate records for observations, approved changes, and verification.
objectives: Identify the information needed in an incident or change record.
Explain why a change should be reviewed, approved, verified, and documented.

vocab.def: A record of a planned modification and its result.
A fact directly noticed or measured.
An idea that has not yet been confirmed by evidence.

sections.heading: A record separates facts from guesses
sections.body: A useful record includes time, affected system, symptom, evidence, action, outcome, escalation, and follow-up. Write what was observed separately from what is suspected.

sections.heading: Controlled changes
sections.body: A classroom change workflow is Request, Review, Approve, Change, Verify, and Document. Control reduces surprises and makes it possible to understand what changed.

sections.heading: Accuracy is technical work
sections.body: Clear records help the next person continue safely. Do not record private learner information or production details in a classroom exercise.

practice.prompt: Complete a synthetic incident record with a timestamp, symptom, two pieces of evidence, a safe next step, and an outcome.

quiz.question: Which statement is an observation?
options: The dashboard showed 82 percent storage use at 10:15
The next change will fix everything
quiz.answer: The dashboard showed 82 percent storage use at 10:15

lab.objective: Complete a structured change or incident record using a provided synthetic scenario.

reflectionPrompt: What detail would help another person understand what happened without guessing?
